report.intro: A demo that makes a sales table from a seed and aggregates it by region into a report. Press ▶ Run and the Cards move in the order they did when it really ran.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.settings: Sends the settings: seed 42, 500 rows and a heading.
cards.share: Hands the same settings to generate and render.
cards.generate: Writes 500 rows of region, product, quantity and unit price as CSV, with random numbers from the seed. The same seed gives the same CSV.
cards.aggregate: Totals sales and quantity per region.
cards.render: Writes the aggregate to report.md and summary.json and shows the report.
cards.archive: The child Workflow inside duplicates the report's folder and files it away.

report.finale: The report was kept as an artifact. What each Card received and output is in the record too.

collatz.intro: A demo that implements the same Collatz iteration separately in C++, Python, Julia and R, and checks that the four sequences agree.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.both: Hands the same value to the four sides: C++, Python, Julia and R.
cards.collatz-cpp: The Workflow inside runs the iteration on its wires, halving even numbers and tripling odd ones plus 1, until it reaches 1.
cards.collatz-py: On the Python side, a Workflow of the same shape runs the same iteration.
cards.collatz-jl: The Julia side has the same shape. It runs in a separate process per invocation, so it carries the sequence so far in the message.
cards.collatz-r: The R side has the same shape. R handles integers exactly only below 2 to the 53rd, so beyond that it fails rather than round silently.
cards.compare: Checks that the four sequences agree exactly.
cards.record: Writes the sequence to collatz.csv and keeps it as an artifact.

collatz.finale: 27 reached 1 in 111 steps, with a maximum of 9232 on the way. The implementations' sequences agree.

live-stream.intro: A demo that makes one value of a random walk every 100 ms and draws it as a line chart in real time.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.settings: Sends the seed, the count, the interval and the first state.
cards.generate: Takes one step, sends the value to plot, and returns the next state to its own input. This loop of wires goes round until the set count.
cards.loop: Merges the first state with the next state coming back from generate.
cards.plot: Draws the latest values and their mean as a line chart.

live-stream.finale: After the set number of values, no next state came out and the stream ended. In the app you can stop it partway, and the chart up to there stays.

plots.intro: A demo that plots random walks with the same matplotlib, Plotly and Altair code you would write anywhere else. No Tsugumi-specific drawing calls are used.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.settings: Sends the seed, the number of walkers and the number of steps.
cards.share: Hands the same walks to the four figures.
cards.summary: Four Cards draw figures from the same walks. Report publishes the Matplotlib animation, Plotly figure and Altair chart through explicit report.figure calls.
cards.diffusion: Draws with FuncAnimation how the distribution spreads as √t.
cards.explore: Makes a Plotly scatter plot of each walker's final position and farthest distance.
cards.spread: Draws with Altair the mean squared distance growing in proportion to t, next to the theory.

plots.finale: Four figures were made. In the app the animation moves, and the Plotly and Altair figures can be zoomed and hovered. Here the same values are drawn simply.

casa.intro: A demo that pins an X-ray observation of the supernova remnant Cassiopeia A and the analysis tool CIAO with Nix, and splits the photons into three energy bands for an RGB image.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.begin: Starts preparing the analysis tool and the observation at the same time.
cards.ciao: Builds the analysis tool CIAO with Nix, pinned by the hash of its source. The build happens only the first time.
cards.load: Uses the observation file pinned by hash. The download happens only the first time; no network while running.
cards.bands: With CIAO's dmcopy, splits the photons into three energy bands and counts them on a grid centred on Cas A.
cards.share: Hands the bands' directory to rgb and spectrum.
cards.rgb: rgb assigns the three bands to R, G and B for an image, and spectrum draws the energy spectrum of the same photons.
cards.spectrum: The spectrum shows which element's lines fell in which colour.

casa.finale: The RGB image and the spectrum are done. In the app you can change the bands or the stretch and rerun just that Card.

gw150914.intro: A demo that extracts the waveform of the gravitational-wave event GW150914 from GWOSC's public data.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.load: Fetches the H1 and L1 strain data and shows their sizes and SHA-256.
cards.whiten: Whitens and band-passes them, and draws the waveform around the event.
cards.chirp: Shifts L1 to overlay H1, and shows the chirp in a spectrogram.

gw150914.finale: In the app you can change the pass band and rerun only the analysis Cards, without fetching again.

protein-6lu7.intro: A demo that examines the binding pocket in the structure of 6LU7 (the SARS-CoV-2 main protease with the inhibitor N3) from RCSB PDB.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.load: Fetches the PDB file and shows its size and SHA-256.
cards.structure: Takes out the coordinates of the Cα atoms and the inhibitor and shows them as a 3D point cloud.
cards.pocket: Tables the residues near the inhibitor and marks them on a contact map.

protein-6lu7.finale: In the app you can change cutoff and rerun only pocket, without fetching again.

exoplanet-transit.intro: A demo that finds an exoplanet's transit in MAST's light curve of Kepler-6.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.load: Fetches the light curve's FITS and shows its size and SHA-256.
cards.detrend: Removes the trend and searches for the period with Box Least Squares.
cards.fold: Folds the phase by the period and finds the planet-to-star radius ratio from the depth of the dip.

exoplanet-transit.finale: In the app you can change window_days and rerun only the analysis Cards, without fetching again.

seismic-trench.intro: A demo that finds a section of the Japan Trench and the b-value from USGS's earthquake catalogue.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.load: Fetches the hypocentres' CSV and shows its size and SHA-256.
cards.section: Cuts out a band of latitude and draws a map of epicentres and a longitude–depth section.
cards.b_value: Plots the cumulative frequency and finds the b-value of the Gutenberg–Richter law by maximum likelihood.

seismic-trench.finale: In the app you can change the band of latitude or mc and rerun only the analysis Cards, without fetching again.

card-guide.intro: The smallest Workflow, made in the chapter on writing Cards by hand.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.settings: Sends the number 21, which you can edit on the Canvas.
cards.multiply: Multiplies the number it receives by factor, outputs the result and shows it on the Card.

card-guide.finale: The result appeared in multiply's display. Inputs and outputs are in the record, and you can change factor and rerun only multiply.

draft.intro: A Draft is a Card that says in words what it receives, what it does and what it passes on. It has no code yet. With "Generate Cards" in the app, the Agent writes code from these words, runs it and checks.

dynamics-draft.intro: Six Drafts that depend on no other. With "Generate Cards" in the app, the Agent splits them among helpers and implements them at the same time.

mnist-classifiers-draft.intro: Implemented up to the data Cards; the seven classifiers and the comparison are Drafts. With "Generate Cards" in the app, the Agent has helpers implement the seven classifiers at the same time, then writes the comparison.

mnist-classifiers.intro: A demo that feeds the real MNIST to seven classifiers at once and compares accuracy and time. Each classifier has its own Nix environment.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.load: Reads the MNIST files pinned by their Nix hash. No network while running.
cards.prepare: Takes a subset keeping the share of each digit, and scales the pixels.
cards.share: Hands the same data to the seven classifiers and the comparison Card.
cards.knn: The seven branches run at the same time. k-nearest neighbours shows the digits it got wrong and their neighbours.
cards.logistic: Logistic regression. Shows each digit's weights as an image.
cards.svm: An SVM with an RBF kernel. Shows the number of support vectors.
cards.forest: A random forest. Shows the pixels that mattered as an image.
cards.boosting: Gradient boosting (xgboost). Shows the error rate by round.
cards.mlp: A fully connected network (torch). Shows how the loss went.
cards.cnn: A small convolutional network (torch). Shows what the first layer picks out.
cards.compare: Waits for every branch, recomputes the accuracies from the predictions to cross-check, and makes a ranking.
cards.views: Hands the comparison's result to three figures.
cards.tradeoff: Plots accuracy against time with Plotly.
cards.recall: Tables recall by model and digit.
cards.hard: Lays out the images many models got wrong.

mnist-classifiers.finale: The seven results are lined up on the same footing. In the app you can change one classifier's settings and rerun just that branch.

newton.intro: A demo that solves z³ − 1 = 0 by Newton's method on the complex plane, to see how the starting point decides where it goes and how fast.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.settings: Sends the polynomial's coefficients and the damping factor.
cards.roots: Finds the roots and their multiplicities from eigenvalues, without Newton's method.
cards.share: Hands the problem to three Cards.
cards.orbits: Draws how the error falls for each starting point.
cards.order: Estimates the order of convergence from the errors and sets it next to the theory.
cards.basins: Starts from every point of a grid and maps which root each reaches.
cards.trouble: Lays out cases that lose quadratic convergence and cases that do not converge.

newton.finale: The map of where points converge is done. In the app you can change where to zoom and rerun just that Card.

pharmacokinetics.intro: Teaching material comparing how concentration moves with the dosing interval, in a model of a made-up drug, "Tsugumicin". The values are not those of any real drug, and this is not medical advice.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.settings: Sends the dosing plans to compare and the made-up drug's values.
cards.simulate: Solves the differential equation and draws the concentration over time.
cards.share: Hands the results to three Cards.
cards.check: Checks the numerical solution against closed forms. Fails if they differ much.
cards.window: Overlays the concentration in the last dosing interval and compares peaks and troughs.
cards.missed: Draws the concentration when doses are missed partway.

pharmacokinetics.finale: The differences between dosing plans are lined up. Again: teaching material from a made-up model.

max-flow.intro: A demo that checks, on a made-up network made from a seed, that the maximum flow equals the minimum cut.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.settings: Sends the seed and the size of the network.
cards.network: Makes a directed graph with capacities.
cards.flow: Finds the maximum flow and draws each edge's flow.
cards.cut: Finds the minimum cut. Fails unless it equals the maximum flow.
cards.share: Hands the results to three Cards.
cards.verify: Checks that another solver and brute force give the same value.
cards.whatif: Raises capacities on and off the cut and compares the maximum flow.
cards.sweep: For every edge, lays out the gain from raising its capacity.

max-flow.finale: It shows which edges to widen to increase the flow. In the app you can try other edges and amounts.

dose-response.intro: A demo that fits a Hill curve to synthetic data of made-up compounds and puts a confidence interval on the EC50. These are not real drugs.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.generate: Makes a synthetic plate with noise on the true curves.
cards.share: Hands the plate to three Cards.
cards.fit: Fits the four parameters and draws the data and the curves.
cards.bootstrap: Finds intervals by bootstrap and checks whether they contain the true values.
cards.compare: Shows the ratio of the two compounds' potencies and its interval.
cards.range: Draws how the interval's width changes with the highest concentration.

dose-response.finale: The true values are known, so you can check on the spot whether they were recovered.

molecules.intro: A demo that finds properties and structural formulas with RDKit from SMILES, strings that write molecules.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.paste: Sends the SMILES of a molecule to try.
cards.properties: Tables molecular weight, logP and more. A SMILES that cannot be read is skipped, with the reason.
cards.share: Hands the properties to three Cards.
cards.structures: Draws the structural formulas side by side.
cards.chemspace: Draws a map of molecular weight and logP with Plotly.
cards.similarity: Makes a heat map of how alike the structures are.

molecules.finale: In the app, paste your own molecule and it joins every Card.

cell-count.intro: A demo that scores ways of counting cells on synthetic images with known answers, and applies the same procedure to a real image of nuclei.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.begin: Hands the run to both the synthetic and the real image.
cards.generate: Makes a synthetic image of cells with known centres.
cards.share: Hands the image and the answers to three Cards.
cards.segment: Separates regions with a threshold and watershed.
cards.score: Matches them with the answers and scores both methods.
cards.sweep: Changes the number of cells and the noise, and tables where it breaks down.
cards.mitosis: Passes a real image of nuclei, pinned by its Nix hash.
cards.real: Applies the same procedure to the real image. There is no ground truth, so it is not scored.

cell-count.finale: What separating touching cells gains is compared in scores.

survival.intro: A demo with the lung cancer trial data of R's survival package, showing how much the same hazard ratio moves with the subjects and the adjustment. An example of statistical method, not advice.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.load: Adds columns to the data and tables a summary of the variables.
cards.share: Hands the data to two branches.
cards.cohort: Chooses subjects by age and the like.
cards.split: Hands the people chosen to two Cards.
cards.km: Kaplan–Meier curves and the log-rank test.
cards.cox: Finds hazard ratios with a Cox model.
cards.specs: Lays out the hazard ratio for each combination of subjects and adjustment in one figure.

survival.finale: Even with the same data, how much the conclusion moves with the choices is laid out.

meta-analysis.intro: An R demo comparing, over 13 trials of the BCG vaccine, how the conclusion moves with the pooling method and the trials left out. An example of statistical method, not advice about vaccination.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.trials: Finds each trial's effect size and variance.
cards.share: Hands the same effect sizes to four analyses.
cards.pool: Pools with fixed and random effects and draws a forest plot.
cards.funnel: Looks for publication bias with a funnel plot.
cards.sensitivity: Lays out the results when each trial is left out, or the estimator changes.

meta-analysis.finale: The conclusion under each choice is laid out. In the app you can try leaving out other trials.

rna-seq.intro: An R demo that finds differentially expressed genes with DESeq2 and edgeR on airway's real data. A cell-culture experiment; it shows no effect of treatment.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.load: Reads the count matrix and gene names.
cards.share: Hands the counts to four Cards.
cards.normalize: Normalises by size factors and compares before and after.
cards.pca: Looks at treatment and cell line by principal component analysis.
cards.volcano: Counts at the thresholds and draws a volcano plot.
cards.thresholds: Tables the number of genes for each combination of thresholds.
cards.top: Looks at the top genes and the ranks of known responsive genes.
cards.edger: Tests the same counts with edgeR.
cards.compare: Overlays the two methods' results to compare them.
cards.design: Lays out how the results change with the design.

rna-seq.finale: It shows that "the number of differentially expressed genes" changes with thresholds and design.

simpson.intro: An R demo that checks, on two real datasets, examples where the overall trend and the trend within strata point in opposite directions.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.branches: Hands the run to two branches.
cards.share: Hands the data to two Cards.
cards.correlate: Splits into strata and finds the correlations.
cards.figure: Overlays the overall line and the lines for each stratum.
cards.survey: Lays out, for each way of splitting, where it reverses.
cards.admissions: Compares Berkeley's 1973 applications by department and overall.
cards.applications: Draws the admission rates with the numbers of applicants.

simpson.finale: Which value to read is not decided by the data alone. The question decides it.

battery.intro: A Julia demo that optimises the charging and discharging of a home battery by dynamic programming, on made-up price data.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.settings: Sends conditions such as capacity and efficiency.
cards.market: Makes consumption, solar and prices. All of it is made-up data.
cards.share: Hands the conditions and data to four Cards.
cards.schedule: Finds the charging and discharging with the lowest bill.
cards.capacities: Compares the saving at other capacities.
cards.tariffs: Runs the same battery under each contract and compares.
cards.check: Checks the result against exhaustive search. Fails if anything is off.

battery.finale: How operation changes with the tariff and the capacity is laid out.

gillespie.intro: A Julia demo that simulates fluctuations in chemical reactions with Gillespie's method and checks them against theory.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.settings: Sends the reaction rates and the number of runs.
cards.share: Hands the conditions to four Cards.
cards.trajectories: Overlays trajectories, their mean and the solution of the rate equation.
cards.stationary: Compares the distribution of end points with the theoretical Poisson distribution.
cards.scaling: Changes the volume and compares the size of fluctuations with theory.
cards.binding: Compares a binding reaction with the exact solution and the rate equation.
cards.check: Checks the results against closed forms. Fails if anything is off.

gillespie.finale: The simulation was confirmed, in numbers, to agree with the theory.

heat-inverse.intro: A Julia demo of an inverse problem, recovering an initial temperature from measured ones, to see what regularisation does. The data is made up.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.settings: Sends the grid, the measurement time and the noise.
cards.forward: Makes the temperature at time T from a made-up initial temperature, with noise added.
cards.share: Hands the measurements to six Cards.
cards.spectrum: Shows which components sink into the noise.
cards.naive: Shows that solving backwards as it is diverges.
cards.reconstruct: Lays out recoveries at the chosen strength, too small and too large.
cards.horizon: Shows that the later the measurement, the more detail is lost.
cards.check: Checks against conservation laws and analytic solutions. Fails if anything is off.

heat-inverse.finale: The naive solution breaks down, and regularisation recovers it: both are laid out.

ecology-models.intro: A Julia demo that fits predator–prey models to the fur records of hares and lynx and compares them.

cards.start: The run begins at the start Card.
cards.share: Hands the records to two Cards.
cards.fit: Fits three models and overlays them on the records.
cards.forecast: Fits up to a year partway and predicts the rest.
cards.fits-share: Hands the fitted results to three Cards.
cards.scores: Tables errors and AICc to compare.
cards.phase: Extends the solutions ahead and compares them in phase diagrams.
cards.check: Checks with the conserved quantity and an existing case study.

ecology-models.finale: Fit and prediction errors can be compared in the same table. In the app you can change the fitting period and rerun just that Card.
